transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
Honestly, I don’t enjoy my job or any of the things I used to love doing anymore, and it’s been like this for weeks. I just feel completely disconnected from everything that used to bring me joy.
Can you tell me more about how long you've been feeling this way, and has it been consistent over the past few weeks or have you had any periods where you felt somewhat better?

This low, heavy feeling has been dragging on consistently for about six months now, starting right after my work project wrapped up. Before that, I actually had periods where I felt the exact opposite—unusually amped up, buzzing with energy, and working late. Looking back, these big swings between being revved-up and feeling deeply down have been happening off and on for several years.

Can you describe more about these periods when you felt 'revved-up' and had lots of energy - did you also experience decreased need for sleep, excessive spending, or impulsive decisions during those times?

During those times, I was buzzing with energy, working late into the night, sketching out ideas at midnight, and taking on tons of extra projects and meetings. I didn't really have issues with excessive spending or impulsive decisions, but I would stay up very late working because I was just too wired and excited to sit still.

Can you estimate how long these 'revved-up' periods typically lasted, and did they always transition into the low, heavy feelings you're experiencing now, or were there times when you returned to a more normal mood in between?

While these swings have been happening off and on for several years, I'm really not sure of the exact duration of those revved-up periods. I'm also not certain if I returned to a completely normal mood in between them, as I've never really tracked them closely.

Can you try to recall if there were any distinct triggers or events that seemed to set off these revved-up periods, and did you notice any significant changes in your mood or behavior when they ended and the low periods began?

These swings have happened off and on for several years, but this last revved-up phase was triggered by taking on a lead role in a major product relaunch at work. Once that project ended and my workload went back to normal, I abruptly crashed into a flat, low mood where I lost all my energy and focus. This heavy downturn has persisted for about six months now.
Can you clarify if your revved-up periods were typically shorter than your low periods, and did you experience any periods of completely normal mood in between these swings?

Yes, the low periods are definitely much longer—this current downturn has dragged on for six months, while the revved-up times are just temporary stretches. When the last high ended, I went straight into feeling flat and down instead of normal. But over the last several years, there have definitely been times of normal mood in between these big swings.
Can you estimate the average duration of your revved-up periods compared to your low periods, and do you think there's a pattern to how often these mood swings occur?

These swings have been happening off and on for several years, with this current low period dragging on for about six months. I'm not entirely sure of the exact average duration of the revved-up periods or if there's a precise pattern to them, but they really seem to stand out during busy, intense times like the product relaunch.
Can you tell me if the revved-up periods have ever lasted as long as four days, and have you experienced at least four of these distinct mood episodes within a single year?

I'm not entirely sure of the exact number of days those revved-up periods lasted, or if I've had four of them in a single year. I just know that these swings have been happening off and on for several years now.

Can you think back to any specific instance where you felt 'revved-up' and try to estimate if it lasted at least four consecutive days, and also consider if you've had multiple such episodes within a year?

Yes, those revved-up periods definitely lasted much longer than four days. During the product relaunch, it went on for weeks where I was constantly buzzing, working late, and full of energy. These swings between high and low periods have been happening off and on for several years now, so I've definitely experienced multiple episodes over time.
Can you confirm if you've experienced at least four of these distinct mood episodes, with at least one of them being a depressive episode lasting for two weeks, within a single year?

I'm not really sure if I've had as many as four distinct episodes within a single year. I do know that these ups and downs have been happening off and on for several years, though. And this current low period has definitely lasted much longer than two weeks—it's been going on for about six months now.

Can you try to recall if you've had any year in the past where you experienced four or more distinct episodes of either the high, revved-up mood or the low, depressive mood, and if so, did any of those episodes last for at least two weeks for the depressive episodes or at least four consecutive days for the high episodes?

I'm really not sure if I've ever had as many as four distinct swings within a single year. However, my low periods definitely last for several months, like this current six-month stretch, and the high periods usually lasted for weeks at a time during major projects.

Can you think back over the past year and try to estimate the total number of distinct episodes, either high or low, that you've experienced, and did any of the high episodes last for at least four consecutive days while any of the low episodes lasted for at least two weeks?

Over the past year, I've mainly noticed just two major phases: the high period during the product relaunch, followed by this current low period. The high phase lasted for several weeks, which is well over four days, and this low period has been dragging on for about six months now.

Can you confirm whether you have experienced at least four distinct mood episodes, with either the high episodes lasting at least four consecutive days or the low episodes lasting at least two weeks, over the course of a year at any point in the past?

I'm really not sure about the exact number of episodes I've had per year or their precise duration in days. However, I can definitely confirm that these mood swings have been happening off and on for several years now.
Can you try to recall if there was ever a year where you didn't experience any of these significant mood swings, either high or low, to help me understand the pattern of your symptoms?

These swings between high and low periods have been happening off and on for several years now. Because they have been recurring for so long, it's really hard to recall a whole year recently where I felt completely stable without experiencing either a high or a low phase.
Can you recall if there has ever been a period of two months or more where you didn't experience any significant mood swings, either high or low, to help clarify the pattern of your symptoms?

I'm not entirely sure about the exact duration of any normal periods I might have had. While there were definitely times when my mood felt more stable, I can't remember if those stretches actually lasted for two months or more.
Have you ever had a period of at least two months where you felt completely stable and didn't experience any significant mood swings, either high or low?

I'm not entirely sure, and I haven't tracked my mood closely enough to know if I've ever had a full two-month stretch of complete stability. It just feels like I've been dealing with these ups and downs off and on for years now.

Can you think of any time in your life, even if it was years ago, when you felt consistently stable for an extended period, without any significant mood swings, to help me understand if you've ever had a prolonged period of normal mood?

I'm not really sure, and I haven't thought about it much before now. Because these mood swings have been happening off and on for several years, it's hard to remember a long, completely stable period in my life.
Can you recall any specific year or period in your life when you felt your mood was consistently stable, without significant swings, for at least a year?
I'm really not sure and I can't recall any specific long stretch of complete stability like that. It feels like these ups and downs have just been happening off and on for several years now.
Have you ever experienced a full year without any significant mood swings, either high or low, to help me understand the overall pattern of your symptoms?

Looking back over the last several years, these ups and downs have been happening off and on pretty consistently. Because of that, I don't think I've had a full year that was completely free of these mood swings.
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt consistently stable for at least a year without experiencing any significant mood swings, either high or low?

Looking back over the last several years, I’ve experienced these big swings between being revved-up and feeling very low off and on. Because of that, I don't think I've really had a solid, stable year without those mood fluctuations.
Can you confirm if you've ever had a period, even if it was years ago, where you felt your mood was consistently stable for at least two years without significant swings?

I'm really not sure, and I don't recall ever having a stable period that lasted for two years without any of these ups and downs. Since these swings have been happening off and on for several years, a long stretch of stability like that doesn't sound familiar to me.

Can you confirm if you have experienced any period in your life, regardless of how long ago, where your mood was consistently stable for at least two years without any significant mood swings, either high or low?

I honestly don't recall ever having a fully stable period lasting as long as two years. These ups and downs have been happening off and on for several years now, so a long stretch of stability like that doesn't sound familiar to me.
Can you think of any factors or circumstances that might have contributed to the stability of your mood during the times when you felt more normal and not experiencing these significant swings?

I'm really not sure, and I haven't ever thought about what specific factors kept my mood stable during those times. I just felt like my usual self, going about my normal routine of work, yoga, and trail hiking, without noticing any particular reason why my mood was stable.
Have you ever experienced a significant life event or change that seemed to trigger the start of these mood swings, or did they seem to begin without any clear cause?

This current low phase definitely seemed to set in right after the intensity of my work's product relaunch wrapped up and things went back to normal. However, these mood swings have actually been happening off and on for several years, and I can't recall any specific life event that triggered them when they first started years ago.

Can you confirm if you have experienced at least four distinct mood episodes, with either the high episodes lasting at least four consecutive days or the low episodes lasting at least two weeks, over the course of a year at any point in the past, to help differentiate between the potential diagnoses of bipolar disorder and persistent mood disorder?

I'm really not sure about the exact number of episodes, like whether I've had four in a single year. But I can definitely confirm that these big swings between being revved-up and feeling very low have been happening off and on for several years.

Can you try to estimate the number of times you've shifted between these high and low mood episodes within a single year, even if it's just an approximate number, to help clarify the pattern of your symptoms?
I'm not really sure of the exact number of times I shift between those moods in a year. However, these big swings between my high and low periods have been happening off and on for several years now.

Can you confirm if you've ever experienced a manic episode, which is a distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood lasting at least one week, to help differentiate between the potential diagnoses?

Yes, I've definitely experienced periods of being abnormally "amped up" and irritable, especially during the product relaunch and off and on for several years. In those "high gear" phases, I felt on top of the world, extremely active, slept less, took on way too many projects, and felt highly distractible and overly confident. I'm not sure if that officially qualifies as a manic episode, but it was a very intense state for me.
During those 'revved-up' periods, did you ever experience any psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations or delusions, or did you ever require hospitalization due to the severity of your symptoms?
No, I have never experienced any hallucinations or delusions during those high periods. I also have never been hospitalized or needed to go to the hospital because of how revved-up I felt.

Can you confirm if you've ever experienced a period of at least four consecutive days where you felt abnormally elevated, expansive, or irritable, and if so, did you experience any symptoms such as decreased need for sleep, more talkative than usual, or involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences?

Yes, those elevated and irritable periods definitely lasted much longer than four days, especially during the product relaunch when it went on for weeks. During those phases, I felt buzzing with energy, worked late into the night sketching ideas at midnight, and snapped at people over minor things. While I didn't engage in highly risky activities with painful consequences, I was extremely overactive, taking on too many projects and unable to sit still.

Can you confirm if you have experienced at least four distinct mood episodes, with either the high episodes lasting at least four consecutive days or the low episodes lasting at least two weeks, over the course of a year at any point in the past, and have these episodes been recurring over several years without any prolonged periods of complete stability?

I can confirm that these big ups and downs have been happening off and on for several years, and this current low period has lasted for about six months now. However, I'm still not sure about the exact number of episodes I've had in a single year or the precise number of consecutive days those high periods lasted.
